court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Suresh v. Sunita — full case name
facts_of_case: The parties were married for 10 years and had two children. The husband sought divorce on the ground of desertion. The wife denied desertion and claimed that she was subjected to cruelty by her husband. The trial court allowed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage is a sacred institution and the parties to it have a duty to maintain its sanctity.
legal_principles.held: The court has consistently held that a marriage is a sacred institution and the parties to it have a duty to maintain its sanctity. It is settled law that a spouse who wilfully abandons his or her partner without reasonable justification can be considered guilty of cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the other spouse has been guilty of cruelty.
legal_principles.held: It is settled law that the burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the other spouse has been guilty of cruelty. The court will not lightly accept a plea of cruelty and requires cogent evidence to establish it.

outcome.final_order: The final order was that the appeal was dismissed and the divorce decree passed by the trial court was confirmed.
